facts.content: Patient has a 3-day worsening headache with baseline constant and intermittent surges rated at 8/10 in intensity.
facts.source_text: CC: 3-day worsening headache; baseline constant with intermittent surges; 8/10

facts.content: Headache is holocranial and worse around the right eye.
facts.source_text: Location: Holocranial, worse around R eye

facts.content: Headache is dull with intermittent sharp pain and has a gradual onset.
facts.source_text: Character: Dull with intermittent sharp; gradual onset; worse on awakening day 2

facts.content: Headache is associated with photopsia at onset, photophobia, nausea, and difficulty focusing.
facts.source_text: Assoc: Photopsia (“shooting lights”) at onset; photophobia; nausea (no vomiting); difficulty focusing

facts.content: Denies vision loss, blurry vision, speech difficulty, limb weakness, neck pain or stiffness, fever, rash, and head injury.
facts.source_text: Denies: Vision loss, blurry vision, speech difficulty, limb weakness, neck pain/stiffness, fever, rash, head injury

facts.content: Work on the computer and recent project stress are possible triggers.
facts.source_text: Triggers/Context: Work on computer; recent project stress (mild)

facts.content: No chronic conditions reported; no prior migraine diagnosis.
facts.source_text: PMH: No chronic conditions reported; no prior migraine dx

facts.content: Mother and sister have migraines; mother's are frequent and seasonal.
facts.source_text: FH: Mother and sister with migraines (mother frequent, seasonal)

facts.content: Ibuprofen used a few times over the last 2 days at 3 tablets per day with minimal relief.
facts.source_text: Meds tried: Ibuprofen “few” over last 2 days; 3 tabs/day; minimal relief

facts.content: No known drug allergies.
facts.source_text: DH: No regular meds; no known drug allergies

facts.content: Lives with 3 housemates and works an IT job with heavy screen use.
facts.source_text: SH: Lives with 3 housemates; IT job (heavy screen use)

facts.content: Wears glasses but has not had a recent eye test.
facts.source_text: SH: wears glasses; no recent eye test

facts.content: Smokes and drinks socially.
facts.source_text: SH: smokes socially; drinks socially

facts.content: Acute headache is likely a migraine without aura versus a probable migraine with visual phenomenon.
facts.source_text: 1) Acute headache, likely migraine without aura vs probable migraine with visual phenomenon

facts.content: Optimize NSAID dosing with ibuprofen up to 400 mg PO q6–8h with food, or consider Rx naproxen.
facts.source_text: Optimize NSAID dosing: ibuprofen up to 400 mg PO q6–8h with food (max 1200 mg OTC/day), OR Rx naproxen (per standard dosing)

facts.content: Consider add-on paracetamol and possibly a short course of codeine if needed.
facts.source_text: Consider add-on: paracetamol; short course codeine if needed

facts.content: Limit acute meds to 2–3 days per week to avoid MOH.
facts.source_text: Limit acute meds to ≤2–3 days/week to avoid MOH

facts.content: Encouraged hydration, regular meals, sleep hygiene, reduction in screen brightness, and rest in a dark room during attacks.
facts.source_text: Hydration, regular meals, sleep hygiene; reduce screen brightness; rest in dark room during attacks

facts.content: Maintain a headache diary including onset, duration, severity, medications, menses, and triggers.
facts.source_text: Headache diary (onset, duration, severity, meds, menses, triggers)

facts.content: Review in 1–2 weeks, or sooner if worsening or persistent.
facts.source_text: Review in 1–2 weeks; sooner if worsening or persistent

facts.content: Discuss prophylaxis if headaches are recurrent or frequent.
facts.source_text: Discuss prophylaxis if recurrent/frequent

facts.content: Seek urgent care for new neurological deficits, vision loss, severe headache, persistent vomiting, fever/neck stiffness, or head injury.
facts.source_text: Urgent care if new neuro deficits, vision loss, severe/worst-ever headache, persistent vomiting, fever/neck stiffness, or head injury
